principles: Reuse existing spawn + capture + binding primitives; build only the missing bridge and the disagreement diff.
The reviewer is read-only and never modifies the code under review.
Fail-closed: any unparseable/mismatched/absent verdict blocks; never soft-accept.
Never promote a raw provider transcript into evidence; extract only structured verdict fields.
No cryptography in this milestone; value is the adversarial joint decision.
drivers: codex 0.141.0 reliably takes the prompt via stdin and emits the verdict on stdout (SPIKE).
runBoundedCodexProvider hides raw stdout by design so a new leaf must own the spawn.
The verdict must bind to the exact materialHash via the existing submitLocalVerdict path.

options.name: stdin-pipe read-only codex + stdout JSON verdict
pros: own bounded spawn keeps runBoundedCodexProvider digest contract intact
cons: must extract JSON from a transcript with headers

options.name: workspace-write file-drop verdict
pros: verdict is a clean on-disk artifact
cons: SPIKE: workspace-write + prompt hung on stdin
write access lets a reviewer modify reviewed code

options.name: reuse runBoundedCodexProvider
cons: returns stdout as a digest only, cannot yield verdict text

chosen: stdin-pipe read-only codex + stdout JSON verdict
rationale: SPIKE confirmed this is the only reliable, read-only-safe channel on codex 0.141.0; keeps the reviewer from modifying code, leaves runBoundedCodexProvider untouched, parses only structured fields. File-drop needs workspace-write (unsafe + hung in spike); runBoundedCodexProvider cannot return the text.

preMortem.scenario: Codex wraps the verdict in prose or markdown fences
preMortem.mitigation: parser extracts the last schema-matching JSON object; if none, fail-closed to a blocked verdict

preMortem.scenario: materialHash the orchestrator computed differs from what Codex reviewed
preMortem.trigger: worktree drift between prompt build and capture
preMortem.consequence: a verdict could bind to the wrong code
preMortem.mitigation: embed materialHash in the prompt and reject a verdict whose materialHash field mismatches (rebinding guard)

preMortem.scenario: the review-only policy flag widens the implementation subprocess path
preMortem.trigger: refusal logic reused instead of a separate narrower flag
preMortem.consequence: codex could be auto-driven to write code
preMortem.mitigation: keep allowRealHostSubprocess refusal for codex intact; add a separate narrower flag + a smoke asserting the impl path stays refused

preMortem.scenario: fake-Codex test seam diverges from real stdin/stdout shape
preMortem.trigger: seam returns a different structure than the spike output
preMortem.consequence: tests pass but real runs fail
preMortem.mitigation: shape the seam to the exact spike output format
